title: Standardized Cross-Era Mathematical & Clean-Room Engineering Lexicon
purpose: Establishes lexical consistency across five historical eras of analytic and arithmetic number theory (1837-2026) and the clean-room empirical methodology used to study and compress machine-verified proofs.

eras.name: Classical Analytic Foundations
eras.summary: From Dirichlet characters and Riemann's analytic continuation to the classical non-vanishing theorems on the boundary of the critical strip.

eras.name: Adelic Harmonic Analysis & Explicit Positivity
eras.summary: Local-global Fourier analysis over adeles, explicit prime-zero summation formulas, Weil's positivity equivalence, and combinatorial 3-AP-free constructions.

eras.name: Multiplicity, Theta Lifts & Automorphic Representations
eras.summary: Stepanov's function-field multiplicity strategy alongside metaplectic Weil representations, smooth p-adic classification, Lie-group factorisation, canonical globalisation, and isobaric rigidity.

eras.name: Regularized Periods, Galois Compatibility & Arithmetic Slopes
eras.summary: Dual reductive pairs, Howe duality, regularized Siegel-Weil identities, seesaw inner products, automorphic purity, local-global Galois compatibility, and Arakelov slope bounds.

eras.name: Integral p-adic Hodge Theory & Machine-Verified Synthesis
eras.summary: Prismatic cohomology, integral Dieudonné lattices, and the complete machine-checked synthesis chaining unitary theta lifts to prove RH and GRH.

terms.plain_definition: A periodic, completely multiplicative weight chi(n) modulo N paired with the series L(s, chi) = sum chi(n) n^{-s}, generalizing the Riemann zeta function to primes in arithmetic progressions.
terms.role_in_proof: Defines the exact family of analytic functions whose non-vanishing for Re(s) > 1/2 is the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH).
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'Dirichlet L-function' consistently rather than mixing 'Dirichlet series' and 'character zeta'.

terms.plain_definition: The vertical region 0 < Re(s) < 1 where all nontrivial zeros reside; Riemann's functional equation reflects zeros symmetrically across the critical line Re(s) = 1/2.
terms.role_in_proof: Combined with Hadamard and de la Vallée Poussin's boundary non-vanishing on Re(s) >= 1, symmetry reduces the entire hypothesis to ruling out zeros with Re(s) > 1/2.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'critical strip' and 'functional symmetry' when describing the reflection s <-> 1-s.

terms.plain_definition: Tate's unified Fourier-analytic integral over all completions (real, complex, and p-adic) of a number field simultaneously.
terms.role_in_proof: Supplies analytic continuation, Euler products, local root numbers, and functional equations for Hecke L-functions in a uniform framework.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'adelic zeta integral' or 'Tate local-global duality'.

terms.plain_definition: An explicit duality relating sums over prime powers to sums over zeros, showing that RH holds if and only if a specific quadratic functional W(f * f~) is non-negative on test functions.
terms.role_in_proof: Serves as the central analytic bridge converting algebraic and automorphic inequalities into zero-free half-planes.
terms.preferred_usage: Always credit both Guinand (1948) and Weil (1952) as the 'Guinand-Weil positivity criterion'.

terms.plain_definition: A dense subset of integers containing no three equally spaced elements, constructed via lattice points on high-dimensional spheres.
terms.role_in_proof: Used in the original 2026 formalization to select parameters for an Iwasawa tower; explicitly flagged by the proof's author as an early candidate for mathematical simplification.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'Behrend progression-free construction' rather than shorthand '3-AP trick'.

terms.plain_definition: A proof strategy originating over finite fields that bounds point counts by constructing an auxiliary object vanishing to high order; over the integers, where differentiation fails to produce arithmetic multiplicity, it is emulated by a long chain of iterated unitary theta lifts.
terms.role_in_proof: Provides the overarching organizing blueprint connecting all automorphic and geometric subsystems of the proof.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'multiplicity paradigm' or 'iterated unitary theta chain'.

terms.plain_definition: A canonical projective unitary representation on a double cover of the symplectic group that generalizes classical theta functions to arbitrary reductive dual pairs.
terms.role_in_proof: Powers every step of the length ~sqrt(X) chain of theta lifts across totally definite unitary groups.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'Weil unitary representation' and 'metaplectic double cover'.

terms.plain_definition: The combined local theory classifying smooth p-adic representations (Bernstein-Zelevinsky), factoring smooth vectors on Lie groups (Dixmier-Malliavin), extending Harish-Chandra modules canonically (Casselman), and enforcing strong multiplicity one (Jacquet-Shalika).
terms.role_in_proof: Pins down local automorphic components and rules out degenerate cancellations in Satake parameter comparisons.
terms.preferred_usage: Refer to the specific constituent theorem by author name rather than generic 'published library'.

terms.plain_definition: An identity expressing regularized theta integrals via special values of Siegel Eisenstein series, paired with Rallis's seesaw mechanism and Gan-Gross-Prasad period formulas to compute inner products.
terms.role_in_proof: Controls the norms and Bessel periods along the iterated theta-lift spine.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'regularized Siegel-Weil identity' and 'seesaw period duality'.

terms.plain_definition: The correspondence attaching pure l-adic Galois representations to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations so local Frobenius data match local automorphic parameters.
terms.role_in_proof: Constructs the integral Galois-representation row that anchors the single largest uniquely dependent branch of the proof graph.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'automorphic Galois compatibility' (Clozel-Caraiani lineage).

terms.plain_definition: Geometric height and lattice-volume inequalities for Hermitian vector bundles over rings of integers, bridging algebraic geometry and Minkowski-style lattice estimates.
terms.role_in_proof: Supplies covolume lower bounds and divisibility estimates across the abelian-variety height machinery.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'Arakelov slope inequality' and 'Bost covolume bound'.

terms.plain_definition: An integral p-adic cohomology structure introduced by Bhatt and Scholze that classifies crystalline lattices and p-divisible groups without inverting p.
terms.role_in_proof: Controls integral inertia eigenvalues and crystalline lattice comparisons inside the abelian-variety height proofs.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'prismatic Dieudonné classification' or 'prismatic integral lattice'.

terms.plain_definition: A strict operational separation in which all measurement, modeling, and experimental trials happen in an isolated laboratory while the verified mathematical proof remains completely untouched until a change passes formal acceptance.
terms.role_in_proof: Prevents speculative experiments from contaminating the verified proof baseline or invalidating build caches.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'clean-room laboratory' and 'verified reference artifact' in scholarly text.

terms.plain_definition: A five-dimensional measurement of proof size capturing module count, source lines, raw bytes, exported kernel proof-term size, and compilation compute cost simultaneously.
terms.role_in_proof: Prevents misleading single-metric optimizations that shrink one dimension (such as compile time) while inflating another (such as import lines).
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'structural mass' or 'five-component mass budget'.

terms.plain_definition: The set of downstream modules that are reachable from the main theorem exclusively through one given module (formally, its subtree in the graph-theoretic dominator tree).
terms.role_in_proof: Measures the exact upper bound on proof mass that can be simplified or eliminated if a single intermediate theorem is replaced by a shorter argument.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'sole-dependency subtree' (noting 'dominator subtree' once at first definition).

terms.plain_definition: A module imported directly by hundreds or thousands of other modules (high direct in-degree / fan-in in the dependency graph).
terms.role_in_proof: Identifies interface-sensitive foundations where even a minor signature change triggers wide recompilation across the proof tree.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'high-impact shared module' (noting 'direct importer count' rather than bare 'fan-in').

terms.plain_definition: Non-mathematical structural lines—blank lines, import headers, namespace openings, compiler directives—and machine-generated wrapper files that merely re-export a theorem proven in an adjacent file.
terms.role_in_proof: Quantifies mechanical size that can be reduced safely without altering the underlying mathematical argument.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'scaffolding overhead' and 'generated forwarding wrapper'.

terms.plain_definition: A two-stage empirical protocol: first conducting a complete observational census of the untouched proof, then evaluating each candidate compression rule on balanced, randomly allocated treatment and control module pairs stratified by domain and file size.
terms.role_in_proof: Measures true net reduction and failure rates objectively before scaling any transformation across the proof tree.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'observational baseline study' and 'stratified controlled trial'.

terms.plain_definition: The explicit contract specifying which core theorem statements and axioms may never change, together with five pass/fail checks (import integrity, acyclicity, zero core drift, compilation of all affected importers, and strict axiom preservation).
terms.role_in_proof: Guarantees that every accepted reduction preserves full mathematical soundness and independent kernel verifiability.
terms.preferred_usage: Use 'interface boundary' and 'five safety invariants' instead of opaque internal gate codes.

terms.term: Independent Clean-Room Derivation vs. Verbatim Copying
terms.plain_definition: The epistemic and provenance distinction between (a) independently arriving at a mathematical theorem, structural invariant, or reduction rule from primary specifications and empirical measurements (convergence), (b) recording factual read-only telemetry and SHA-256 structural fingerprints, and (c) verbatim copying of unlicensed upstream proof source bodies into an MIT-licensed laboratory.
terms.role_in_proof: Reconciles UP-08 so independent clean-room verification, structural fingerprinting, and original proof synthesis remain encouraged while verbatim proof-body copying into SCargo remains strictly prohibited.
terms.preferred_usage: Distinguish 'independent clean-room derivation' and 'empirical structural telemetry' explicitly from 'verbatim source copying'.
